scientific_limits.en: {"representation":"living-reconstruction","scope":"Whole Placodus gigas living reconstruction using Senckenberg original skeletal remains, supplementary reconstructed mount and species-specific tooth evidence. Not a single pristine complete skeleton or a specimen scan.","scientific_limits":{"en":"The Senckenberg mount contains large missing intervals, especially the tail; Zurich is explicitly a reconstructed mount. Museum size1.5m and Paul estimated total3.2m differ and cannot be asserted as matching measurements: use3.2m nominal restored total, not precise measured length. Soft tissues, webbing, color and distal tail shape are inferred. A humerus historically included by Drevermann was reassigned to Nothosaurus by Rieppel1994 and must not be copied. Palatal specimen BSP1968I75 is a different individual, not the skeleton skull.","zh":"森肯贝格架有大量缺段，尤其尾部，苏黎世明确是重建架。博物馆尺寸1.5米与Paul估计总长3.2米不同，不得宣称一致实测；采用3.2米名义补全总长而非精密长度。软组织、蹼、颜色及末尾形状推定。Drevermann纳入的一枚肱骨被Rieppel1994改归Nothosaurus，不照抄。BSP1968I75齿板为另一个体，不冒骨架同一头骨。"},"name":{"en":"Placodus","zh":"Placodus（海生爬行类）"},"taxon":"Placodus gigas","classification":"Reptilia; Sauropterygia; Placodontia; Placodontidae","era":"triassic","reconstruction_type":"whole-organism","original_scope":{"en":"Planned animal asset: deep barrel torso and projecting front teeth ahead of crushing plates.","zh":"规划中的动物资产：深桶躯干与压碎齿板前方突出的前齿。"},"evidence_anchors":{"body":"Daderot2012 photograph of original Senckenberg mounted bones: deep curved ribs/gastralia forming barrel trunk, short neck, four limb positions and single midline row of low round osteoderms. Missing bones/support rods are not anatomy.","complete_layout":"NGPezz2021 Zurich reconstructed mount: supplementary full outline/limb layout only, not original complete fossil or independent measured scale. Retain uncertainty of reconstructed tail.","dentition":"Gere et al2024 Fig1 actual BSP1968I75 palatal cranium,2cm bars: large flattened palatine and smaller marginal maxillary teeth. Text explicitly three premaxillary pairs, four maxillary pairs and three palatine pairs in P.gigas. Front teeth project forward, posterior crushing teeth not pointedfangs.","classification":"Klein et al2022 supports P.gigas context but new isolated dentaries assigned only cf.gigas; do not adopt those as definitive same individual. Historical P.antiquior synonymy acknowledged.","limb_correction":"Rieppel1994 Fig60A is Nothosaurus formerly attributed to Placodus; Fig60B SMNS59827 is P.gigas, C MHI776 Placodus. Neither rescales the whole model.","scale":"Paul supplementary table SMF R1035 estimates3.2m; museum original exhibit lists1.5m without resolving full restored total vs preserved display extent. Record both, do not silently average or convert1.5 into an exact total."},"scale":{"unit":"metre","nominal_inferred_total_length":3.2,"museum_listed_size":1.5,"basis":"Paul estimated complete length SMFR1035; museum size discrepancy retained and unresolved, not same measured quantity claimed.","inferred_targets":{"head_length":0.36,"head_width":0.23,"head_height":0.19,"neck_length":0.26,"barrel_trunk_length":1.2,"trunk_max_width":0.52,"trunk_max_depth":0.58,"tail_length":1.38,"limb_root_to_tip_range":[0.32,0.43],"front_tooth_visible_projection_range":[0.025,0.05]},"interpretation":"Subordinate targets are conservative modeling ratios from original ribcage and reconstructed outline, not measurements of preserved individual. Tail uncertainty does not erase original deepbody/frontteethgate."},"morphology":["Deep rounded barrel torso with substantial ventral volume, short distinct neck and robust moderately elongated head. No flattening into a turtle shield or generic ichthyosaur fusiformbody.","Three pairs of short sturdy forward-projecting upper premaxillary teeth, chisel-like tips, not thin predatoryfangs or giantwalrustusks. Show them clearly in lateral and head-on views. Lower anterior dentition simplify conservatively as two pairs of short grasping teeth, a reconstructed working arrangement rather than a measured skeleton count.","Behind the anterior grasping teeth, four pairs of smaller flattened upper marginal teeth and three pairs of broad flat palatal crushing teeth. Do not turn the entire toothrow into pointedcrocodilefangs. Lower cheek dentition is rounded/flat crushing surfaces.","Modestly open jaws around20degrees to make frontteeth and posteriorflat crushing surfaces inspectable without grotesque gape; maintain thick lips/gums and fully fleshedhead, not bare skull.","Four stout splayed limbs ending in five short digits each, light partialwebbing inferred, no sea-turtle flippers. Keep elbows/knees and shortforearm transitions, do not recreate misassigned nothosaur bone.","Single row of low rounded dorsal osteoderms integrated along midline, not tallspines and not a broad shell. Long tapering muscular tail with no fishfluke/dorsalfin; restored length/terminalshape explicitly inferred.","Subdued gray-brown skin with slightly darker back and low osteoderms; exact color/scalation unknown. No specimen supports, exposedribs or extrahead."],"shape_gate":{"required_combination":"Deep barrel trunk plus conspicuous forward short anterior grasping teeth in front of broad posterior crushing surfaces, whole body retained.","comparisons":"Cyamodus has two broad armour shields and compact broadhead; Placodus has no broadcarapace, a single low dorsalrow, deeper unshieldedbarrel and protrudingfrontteeth. Simosaurus has longerneck and different blunt-tooth arrangement, not the Placodus projectingchisel front plus palatal pavement.","acceptance":["Lateral clearly deep barrel torso, shortneck and forward chisel-like frontteeth.","Head-on and perspective reveal anterior-to-posterior tooth differentiation without giantfangs.","Top shows no turtlecarapace/two-shield transplant; exactlyfour shortleggedlimbs and single low dorsalosteodermrow.","No Nothosaurus misassigned diagnostic limb copy, no precisionclaim on restoredtail or3.2m estimate."]}}
